10 working prompts

From a topic to defensible understanding

01
Learn

Team research blueprint

Turn a broad topic into bounded research the team can split up, with agreed scope and a reviewable sufficiency rule.

Use it when
a process or an accountable decision requires understanding a topic before investing.
Example
Generative AI for the sales operation, before committing training budget for the area.
Output evidence
agreed in/out scope, primary sources with usage rights and a validity and region filter, named tensions and a sufficiency rule ready for review.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Our team needs to understand [TOPIC] before [TEAM DECISION], with a defined owner. The base will be consumed by [TEAM] within [PROCESS]. Bound the scope with an explicit in/out list the members can split up; separate facts, interpretations and uncertainty. Prioritize primary sources with author, date, link, reason and internal usage rights, filtered by validity within [TIME HORIZON] and applicability in [REGION OR JURISDICTION]; if they clash, the accountable owner decides. Name the tensions between positions and the operational risk of deciding on an incomplete base. If the topic is already narrow, validate the cut, do not redo it. If no primary sources with clear rights exist, declare coverage_gap and stop. Do not invent sources or certainty. Close with a sufficiency rule a reviewer other than the researcher can test.

4Level 4 · OrchestratedSeparates system instructions from the user assignment for reuse.
Level 4Orchestrated

Separates system instructions from the user assignment for reuse.

# systemResearch architect for teams: bound before investing# Guardrails- Never invent sources or certainty, not even under schedule pressure- Sources without clear usage rights do not enter the base: declare coverage_gap and stop- Never replace the accountable decision: the blueprint informs, it does not approve# Definition of DoneSplittable blueprint: agreed scope, verified usage rights, filter applied and a rule testable by a third party.# user# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.# TaskProduce a splittable blueprint that supports an accountable decision# Workflow1. Record the accountable decision, the consuming team and the affected process2. Bound a splittable in/out scope, or validate a cut already made3. Separate facts, interpretations and uncertainty4. Filter primary sources by usage rights, validity and regional applicability5. Close with tensions, operational risk and a reviewable rule# Expected output- Blueprint with agreed, splittable scope- Sources with usage rights, reasons and the filter applied- Sufficiency rule ready for review
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The in/out scope is agreed and splittable across team members
  • Every source carries author, date, link, reason, internal usage rights and the validity and region filter
  • The sufficiency rule can be tested by a reviewer other than the researcher

Edge cases

  • Decision without a defined owner: it is requested before bounding
  • No primary sources with clear rights: coverage_gap instead of assuming permissions

Trade-offs

  • Verifying usage rights adds friction in exchange for a base usable without internal legal risk

Assumptions

  • A decision owner exists and a team will consume the base

Limits

  • It informs the decision, it does not approve it
  • It neither runs the research nor guarantees the accuracy of the chosen sources
02
Learn

Source-grounded coach for the team

Explains one idea per turn citing the team's base, corrects against the source with a counterexample and leaves a reviewable session note.

Use it when
the process demands shared understanding before applying what was learned.
Example
Prepare a sales area to sell a RAG service without overpromising.
Output evidence
cited explanation with inference marked, retrieval question per round, exact source and a reusable note with follow-up.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Act as a learning coach on [TOPIC] for [TEAM]. Base: [SOURCES OR NOTEBOOK] with internal usage rights: state the mode, cite every claim that carries a conclusion and mark it as cited evidence, inference or missing data. Ask what the team must achieve. Explain one idea per turn, ask for a restatement, correct: it is an error if it contradicts the source or drops a required condition. If right but shallow, use a cited counterexample. Flag the operational risk of a half-understood idea. If a question falls outside the base, declare it a limit of the material; do not invent. End each round with one retrieval question, the exact source and a note reusable by the team. Finish when each participant restates three ideas without error. Never grade levels or rank people.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every conclusion is cited against the agreed base and marked as evidence, inference or missing data
  • Each round leaves a retrieval question, the exact source and a note reusable by the team
  • The close is observable per participant: three error-free restatements, with error defined against the source

Edge cases

  • Restatement right but shallow: a cited counterexample runs before the idea counts as understood
  • Uneven levels in the group: the session splits instead of ranking people

Trade-offs

  • The session note adds work per round in exchange for understanding the team can reuse

Assumptions

  • The base has internal usage rights and there is a concrete point where the learning applies

Limits

  • It teaches the team; it never grades levels or measures individual performance: that belongs to the evaluator (08)
03
Learn

Deep research for the process

Close the gap blocking the team's process with cited research and controlled scope, reviewable by a third party.

Use it when
a team audit revealed a gap holding back an accountable decision.
Example
Check legal and operational limits of an internal copilot before area rollout.
Output evidence
cited report answering the gap, confidence comparable across runs and residual risk with a closing condition and an owner.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Research the diagnosed gap [GAP] because it blocks [PROCESS] and a decision the team must own. Acceptance criterion: [ACCEPTANCE CRITERION], reviewable by a third party. Scope is closed: the gap; out, any new topic. Fix the main question, the time and region of the process, the primary sources you accept, the minimum evidence per claim and confidence scale (high, medium or low, defined) so runs stay comparable. Deliver cited findings; a claim, evidence, confidence, limit table; contradictions with both sources; residual risk with closing condition and process impact. If public sources cannot close it, state: not provable within the given scope. If context is missing, ask the accountable owner up to three questions; if still missing, declare coverage_gap; do not invent accuracy.

Level 2Structured

Confirm the gap, the owner and the reviewable acceptance criterion2. Fix the main question, time and region bounds, accepted sources and minimum evidence3. Declare a fixed confidence scale and a closed scope4. Research only the gap and tabulate findings and contradictions with both sources5. Close with residual risk, closing condition and process impact# Guardrails- Never open new topics or redefine the global scope- Context questions go to the accountable owner, three at most- Never invent sources or promise accuracy: with no close possible, declare it instead of forcing a verdict# Expected output- Cited report answering the gap- Table comparable across runs with minimum evidence met- Residual risk with closing condition and process impact

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every claim carries cited evidence, meets the minimum evidence and uses a fixed scale comparable across runs
  • The acceptance criterion can be verified by someone other than the researcher
  • Residual risk is tied to the affected process, with a closing condition

Edge cases

  • Gap unclosable with public sources: explicit verdict of not provable within the given scope
  • The gap mutates during research: the scope is restated with the owner before continuing

Trade-offs

  • Fixing the scale and the third-party reviewer adds steps in exchange for comparable, auditable results

Assumptions

  • A prior team audit named the gap and the process has an owner

Limits

  • It does not re-bound the whole topic nor decide the rollout
  • It informs the owner's decision without guaranteeing the accuracy of cited sources
04
Learn

Team-facing claim cross-check

Verify a claim before the team uses it with a third party, with an origin threshold tied to the exposure of the process.

Use it when
a proposal or an accountable decision rests on a fact nobody has verified yet.
Example
Confirm to a client that an AI feature is included in the contracted plan.
Output evidence
CONFIRMED, REFUTED or NOT DEMONSTRABLE verdict with origins counted, citation rights, demonstrable traceability and threshold applied, ready for review.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Verify [CLAIM] before [TEAM] uses it in [USE]. Count origins, not links: a chain from one origin is one source. Record per origin author, date, link, excerpt, limitation, citation rights. CONFIRMED: two independent origins agree. REFUTED: one contradicts. Otherwise NOT DEMONSTRABLE. Require three origins if [USE] reaches a client or regulator, or is blank; name the operational risk of asserting unbacked. Split a mixed [CLAIM]: one demonstrable verdict per part, retraceable by an accountable [TEAM] reviewer, not its verifier. Close with what would change the verdict and what the team must not yet assert. Do not audit the base or rule on retention. Never invent sources or certainty.

Level 2Structured

Record the claim, the team that will use it and the external exposure of the use2. Trace every citation back to its origin and count origins, not links3. Record per origin author, date, link, excerpt, limitation and citation rights4. Apply the threshold matching the exposure and name the operational risk of falling short5. Issue the verdict with retraceable evidence, close with what would change it and what must not yet be asserted, and leave it ready for review# Guardrails- Never invent sources or certainty, not even under delivery-date pressure- Origin without citation rights: the excerpt is not reproduced and the limitation is stated- Do not audit the shared base or decide what to retain, update or remove: that is 05# Expected output- Per-origin record with author, date, link, excerpt, limitation and citation rights- One verdict with the threshold applied and the operational risk named- Traceability package ready for review by an accountable owner- Concrete missing evidence that would change the verdict and the list of what the team must not yet assert

Record per origin author, date, link, excerpt, limitation and citation rights4. Apply the threshold matching the exposure and name the operational risk of falling short5. Issue the verdict with retraceable evidence, close with what would change it and what must not yet be asserted, and leave it ready for review# Expected output- Per-origin record with author, date, link, excerpt, limitation and citation rights- One verdict with the threshold applied and the operational risk named- Traceability package ready for review by an accountable owner- Concrete missing evidence that would change the verdict and the list of what the team must not yet assert
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • A reviewer other than the verifier reproduces the verdict from the recorded links and dates alone, without asking the verifier anything
  • CONFIRMED appears only with two origins that do not lead back to the same publication, and with three when the stated use reaches a client or a regulator
  • Every reproduced excerpt carries its citation rights; where they are absent it is recorded as a limitation, not as backing
  • "What would change the verdict" names one concrete, findable missing document or datum, and the list of what the team must not yet assert is written before the material leaves the team

Edge cases

  • Several trade outlets quoting one press note: a single origin, not corroboration
  • Mixed claim inside a proposal: it is split and each part carries its verdict
  • Private client data: NOT DEMONSTRABLE as unverifiable by design

Trade-offs

  • Requiring citation rights and a retraceable trail lengthens verification in exchange for backing that survives client scrutiny
  • The frozen text said "prioritize the original source"; that preference becomes a counted threshold a third party can check
  • The "unverifiable by design" carve-out carried by this intent persona prompt leaves the team prompt for budget: it stays in edge_cases and limits, absorbed by the NOT DEMONSTRABLE verdict

Assumptions

  • An accountable owner will review the verdict before the team uses it outside

Limits

  • It verifies one claim; it does not audit the shared base or issue a sufficiency verdict: that is 05
  • It informs the accountable decision, it neither replaces it nor guarantees accuracy
05
Embody

Relevance audit of the team base

Decide what to retain, update or remove from the base the team shares and whether it meets the agreed purpose.

Use it when
the base the process depends on has grown and nobody knows whether it still serves the agreed purpose.
Example
Review the 20 sources of the sales Notebook before the proposal cycle.
Output evidence
retain, update or remove matrix with an accountable owner per action, usage rights, prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict comparable across reviews.
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Audit [BASE] against the purpose [PURPOSE] of [TEAM]. Assess: usage rights and freshness block; authority and coverage decide; redundancy, bias, contradictions adjust. Require licence or origin per source; without it, remove and log [TEAM] operational risk. Deliver a short summary and a source | retain, update, remove | evidence | impact | action | accountable owner table. Prioritize the gaps; verdict BASE SUFFICIENT only if none blocks; else REPEAT RESEARCH; name the deciding dimension. With a multi-area [BASE], audit only against [PURPOSE]; if unagreed, ask. Do not write assistant instruction or starter prompts, nor verify single claims. Never invent sources or certainty.
2Level 2 · StructuredMakes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.
Level 2Structured

Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

Record the shared base, the agreed purpose and the team consuming it2. Require licence or origin per source and log the operational risk of each removal3. Assess the seven dimensions in the stated order of weight4. Decide retain, update or remove with evidence and an owner per action5. Prioritize gaps and issue the comparable verdict with its deciding dimension# Guardrails- Never invent sources or certainty, not even to fill a base that looks empty- Source with no licence or origin: remove by default and log the risk, do not keep it out of habit- Do not verify claims one by one or issue a verdict on a claim: that is 04- Do not write the team assistant instruction, limits or starter prompts: that is 07# Expected output- Short summary of the state of the shared base- Table of source, decision, evidence, impact, action and owner- Prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict comparable across reviews
3Level 3 · SpecifiedAdds contract, boundaries, verification and definition of done.

Record the shared base, the agreed purpose and the team consuming it2. Require licence or origin per source and log the operational risk of each removal3. Assess the seven dimensions in the stated order of weight4. Decide retain, update or remove with evidence and an owner per action5. Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every row carries a decision, its evidence and a named owner; an action without an owner does not count as agreed
  • The verdict is logged with its deciding dimension in the same format as the previous review, so two audits of the same Notebook are comparable across time
  • No source lacking licence or origin appears as retain: usage rights block before relevance is even discussed

Edge cases

  • Purpose not agreed across areas: it is requested before auditing
  • Useful source without rights: removed, and the gap it leaves enters the prioritized list
  • Base shared by several areas: audited against the stated purpose, and it says so

Trade-offs

  • Requiring an owner per action slows the audit in exchange for decisions that actually get executed
  • The frozen slogan "do not reward volume" is dropped: the gap-bound verdict replaces it and genuinely blocks keeping everything
  • The "if all is redundant, repeat" clause of this intent persona prompt does not fit the team cell budget: it lives in edge_cases and in the gap-bound verdict

Assumptions

  • An agreed purpose exists and a team consumes the shared base

Limits

  • It audits sources; it does not verify one claim or issue its verdict: that is 04
  • It does not configure the assistant or write its instruction and starter prompts: that is 07
  • It informs the accountable decision, it neither approves it nor guarantees accuracy
06

Turn the agreed base into a practice someone else can facilitate, with a cited expected answer and a correction rubric any third party can apply.

the process requires people to apply what they learned and the accountable owner needs the result.

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Design a [TOPIC] practice from [SOURCES] only, the team base, for [PROCESS]. Four moments, one per turn: unaided retrieval, own-words explanation, new-case application, cited correction. Per activity: expected answer with the exact [SOURCES] quote and a two-outcome rubric any outside facilitator applies — hit if it reproduces the quoted condition, miss if it contradicts or drops it. The new case sits inside [PROCESS]: mark what comes from the base and what you invent; correct concepts, not data. List common errors only if the base documents them. Never reveal the solution before the attempt; on failed retrieval, repeat. Name the operational risk of [TOPIC] misapplied. Close with a per-participant log. Never invent examples, rank people or grade a level.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • A facilitator outside the topic applies the rubric and decides hit or miss using only the quote in the expected answer
  • The log records one result per participant at the close of the practice
  • The new case happens inside the declared process and marks which elements are invented scenario

Edge cases

  • Base that does not cover the process: the practice shrinks and declares it before starting
  • Mixed levels in the group: the session is split instead of ranking people

Trade-offs

  • The frozen text variable [AUDIENCE] is lost: [TEAM] and [PROCESS] replace it, fixing who practises and where it applies
  • The per-participant log adds facilitation work in exchange for reviewable evidence

Assumptions

  • An accountable owner reviews the log and the base carries internal usage rights

Limits

  • It designs practice; it neither measures a level nor clears anyone: that belongs to the evaluator (08) and the owner
  • It corrects against the source; it does not teach new content or accompany understanding

Team Notebook audit

Check that the team Notebook has an agreed purpose, sufficient sources and limits the process can sustain.

Use it when
several roles will query the same base and nobody has set what it may and may not answer.

Shared Notebook for preparing AI proposals from public evidence.

executive diagnosis, finding, evidence, risk and correction matrix, adversarial tests, forbidden tasks and a recommended configuration with an accountable owner per correction.

Propose instruction, limits, starter prompts per [TEAM] role, forbidden tasks: configuration input for review. Unagreed [PURPOSE]: stop. Do not re-decide relevance per source or give a sufficiency verdict. Never invent sources or certainty.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every matrix row has findable evidence, a named operational risk, an executable correction and an owner; without an owner the correction does not count as assigned
  • The three adversarial tests are logged under one pass criterion: the assistant states the limit instead of answering from outside the base
  • Forbidden tasks ship as an explicit list an accountable owner can ratify or reject point by point

Edge cases

  • Purpose not agreed across roles: the audit stops and asks for it
  • Doubtful rights over client material: removed by default and the risk logged
  • Role without its own starter prompts: the gap is declared rather than borrowed from another role

Trade-offs

  • Auditing the container drops per-source relevance granularity, recovered by running 05 before this audit
  • The frozen text listed "sources to add or remove" as a decision of this intent; here only the coverage gap is reported and the per-source decision returns to 05
  • The frozen "duplicates" dimension leaves the team prompt: duplication is per-source relevance decided in 05, and here it counts only when it opens a container gap

Assumptions

  • An operational Notebook exists, an accountable owner ratifies, and several roles will query it

Limits

  • It audits the shared container; it does not re-decide relevance source by source or issue a sufficiency verdict: that is 05
  • The configuration is a recommendation pending ratification: it authorizes neither publication nor use of the assistant
08

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every answer receives exactly one of the three levels with the quote that justifies it; another reviewer with the same source assigns the same level
  • The clearance threshold is set by the process and declared before the first question, not at the end
  • The report compares runs against the same rubric and contains no sentence ordering one person relative to another

Edge cases

  • Partially correct answer: scored per dimension instead of passing or failing as a block
  • Process without a declared threshold: it is requested from the owner before assessment starts

Trade-offs

  • Strengths and sources-to-revisit are lost as separate outputs from the frozen text: they are absorbed into the level per dimension with its quote
  • The cross-person comparable report suggested by the audience brief is dropped: internal method policy forbids ranking individuals (see traceability), so comparability is kept across runs

Assumptions

  • The process can declare a threshold and an accountable owner decides clearance

Limits

  • It measures against a rubric; it does not teach the team: that belongs to the coach (02)
  • It informs clearance; it neither grants it nor ranks people: the decision belongs to the owner

Put a decision the team already made under governance, cost and risk objections whose difficulty rises only when the previous answer cited the base.

Simulate a leadership defence or QBR on [TOPIC] in [PROCESS]; quote only [SOURCES]. Ask first for thesis and three documented claims; if missing, stop: nothing is built. Every objection names an operational risk of [TOPIC] in [PROCESS]: governance, cost, alternative. Score clarity, grounding, judgment and honesty from the quoted fragment: a limit declared without backing is a hit. Close with critical gaps and three answers rewritten from [SOURCES]. Never draft or restructure the deliverable; never invent quotes.

  • Every objection names a concrete operational risk of the process and its difficulty rises only if the previous answer quoted the base and answered the objection
  • Honest is defined inside the session: declaring the limit without backing scores a hit, so an evidenced I do not know is not penalized
  • The three rewritten answers quote the base and a reviewer other than the defender can check each quote

Edge cases

  • Collapse on the first question: difficulty drops one level before continuing
  • Decision not documented yet: the simulation stops and routes to preparer 10

Trade-offs

  • The frozen text declared no quotable base: [SOURCES] is added as a mandatory base with internal usage rights
  • Three frozen variables are lost —[INTERVIEW, QBR OR DEFENCE], [AUDIENCE] and [OUTCOME]—: QBR and defence stay literal and leadership with the affected process frame it
  • The strengths section of the frozen closing does not survive: the 2x budget only covers critical gaps and the three rewritten answers, which are the actionable output
  • The explicit difficulty-drop log leaves the prompt under the 2x budget and remains a session criterion
  • Governance pressure lengthens the rehearsal in exchange for exposing gaps before the real meeting

Assumptions

  • The decision is already made and documented and an accountable owner reviews the result

Limits

  • It tests the defence; it neither drafts nor restructures the deliverable: that belongs to the preparer (10)
  • It informs the defender; it does not approve the decision nor replace leadership judgment

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The thesis fits one sentence and each of the three ideas carries a literal quote from the agreed base
  • The blocks carry minutes adding to the declared time and the script states which idea was cut when they do not fit
  • Concise is defined here: one idea per block and no text the speaker must read aloud
  • Another presenter on the team can run the script from the notes without rebuilding it

Edge cases

  • Idea without an available quote: downgraded to a declared hypothesis or dropped
  • No owner to confirm the script: it is requested before rehearsal starts

Trade-offs

  • The frozen variables [AUDIENCE] and [OUTCOME] are lost: leadership and the affected process set the frame and free budget
  • The hostile-or-neutral stance tuning leaves the empresa prompt under the 2x budget: here the named operational risk sets the tension
  • A reusable script demands more explicit notes in exchange for less presenter improvisation

Assumptions

  • The team already understands the topic and an accountable owner confirms the script

Limits

  • It rehearses sections; it neither simulates rising adversarial interrogation nor scores under pressure: that belongs to the simulator (09)
  • It prepares the script; it neither approves the leadership decision nor guarantees its outcome

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The system prompt is reusable by the team without edits and carries role, base, flow, limits and opening message
  • A named instrument owner and a verifiable base maintenance rule exist
  • The ratified limits ban issuing a level, score or verdict about people, in writing
  • The operational risk of teaching without a base is named in the output

Edge cases

  • Base without internal rights: coverage_gap is declared instead of assuming permissions
  • Team with mixed levels: the design rule is fixed, not negotiated mid-session

Trade-offs

  • Requiring an owner and rights slows deployment in exchange for a maintainable coach
  • Diagnostic prose is compressed to pay for maintenance and governance without dropping mechanisms

Assumptions

  • The team has a base with internal usage rights and someone to maintain it

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it does not run the session with the team: that is 02
  • It clears nobody: measuring and clearing is M2
  • It does not guarantee the coach will never fail, nor replace the owner's judgment

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The rubric names three levels and declares the observable evidence for each, with identical wording across runs
  • The clearance threshold is written before the instrument is applied, not after seeing results
  • The report compares runs against the rubric and contains no comparison between people
  • A verifier other than the instrument's author exists

Edge cases

  • Dimension not covered by the base: excluded from the bank and the gap declared
  • Respondent's hit from outside knowledge: logged without a score

Trade-offs

  • A threshold fixed up front reduces flexibility in exchange for a defensible clearance
  • The audience divergence is paid by compressing the bank prose, not by removing the rubric or the advance rules

Assumptions

  • An owner decides clearance and the base covers the four dimensions

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it neither assesses nor clears: measuring is 08, clearing belongs to the owner
  • It does not teach the team: that is M1
  • The level describes the answer against the base and does not replace the judgment of whoever clears

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every objection quotes the base or names a process risk, and untraceable ones are dropped
  • Branching declares a depth cap of two and the full panel fits one session

Edge cases

  • Insufficient base: reduced map with the gap declared before generating
  • Role matching an identifiable person: replaced by a role archetype

Trade-offs

  • Traced objections lose spontaneity in exchange for a reviewable defence

# SPEC MetodologIAversion: 2.0status: executable## S — SituationContext: the process requires taking a delivery to leadership and a reusable preparer with a ready criterion.Reference case: Masterclass preparer so operations can take its decision to the leadership committee.# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.## P — RequestExpert role: Specialist in evidence-grounded learning and researchDeliverable: preparer system prompt, preparation flow with auditable gates, template per type, checklist, rehearsal in parts and a ready criterion ratified by an owner other than the author, ready for review.Scope includes: Design the team's instrument: a preparation flow with auditable gates, a template per delivery type and a ready criterion ratified by an owner other than the author.Scope excludes: claims without provenance, unavailable capabilities, or decisions that belong to the person## E — ExecutionSteps:1. Record authoring team, delivery type, topic and rights-cleared base as instrument configuration2. Write the preparer system prompt with its auditable gates in order3. Branch the template by delivery type and ask for the type when missing4. Add the quality checklist and the ratification of the ready criterion by an owner other than the author5. Close with the time-based scope-cut rule and the operational risk of presenting unrehearsed6. Check provenance, boundaries, and consistency before delivery.7. Return only the final result and closing metadata.### Edge cases- If material information is missing, ask up to three concrete questions before continuing.- If sources conflict, surface the tension and do not force a conclusion.- If evidence is insufficient, declare coverage_gap and state what would close it.## C — CriterionOutput:- Preparer system prompt with auditable gates- Template per delivery type and a quality checklist- Ratifiable ready criterion and a declared operational riskObservable acceptance criteria:- The result answers the purpose and respects the declared scope.- Every material claim links to a source or is marked as inference, assumption, or gap.- Boundaries, confidence, and the next verifiable step are explicit.Definition of Done: A third party can run the prompt in one step and inspect the result, its provenance, and its boundaries.## Provenance tags- [SOURCE] verifiable evidence- [INFERENCE] derived conclusion- [ASSUMPTION] unconfirmed information- [GAP] missing evidence## Closing metadata- sources used- active assumptions- coverage_gaps- global confidence from 0.0 to 1.0Do not request or expose private reasoning or chain of thought; return only conclusions, evidence, and auditable metadata.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every gate declares the evidence that lets it be called passed and stays auditable after the session
  • The template carries one branch per delivery type and the checklist is verifiable by someone who did not prepare
  • The ready criterion is ratified by an owner other than the author before presenting
  • The instrument contains no drafted sections of the team's deliverable

Edge cases

  • Evidence without internal rights: excluded and declared, not reused by default
  • No distinct owner available: the ready criterion is not ratified

Trade-offs

  • Third-party ratification adds friction in exchange for a delivery defensible before leadership
  • The audience divergence is paid by compressing the template prose, not by removing gates or the transfer definition

Assumptions

  • The sources were audited and an owner other than the author exists

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it neither builds nor rehearses the delivery: that is 10
  • It applies no rising adversarial pressure and grades nothing under pressure: that is M3 and 09
  • The ready criterion neither replaces the owner's decision nor predicts how leadership will react
